title: Reducing On‑Call Latency with WakeUp Dev: Voice‑First Alerting from Grafana
description: Integrate Grafana alerts into WakeUp Dev, use voice ACKs, unlimited seats, and pay‑per‑alert to cut response times and cost.
author: Enrique Drack
topic: Reducing On‑Call Latency with WakeUp Dev: Voice‑First Alerting from Grafana

blocks.text: Integrating Grafana alerts into a voice‑first on‑call platform can dramatically reduce the time between detection and acknowledgement. WakeUp Dev’s webhook‑first architecture lets you push alerts directly from Grafana to a phone cascade, eliminating the need for email or chat notifications that often get buried.

Grafana’s webhook integration is straightforward: configure the alert rule to POST to https://api.wakeupdev.com/v1/alert with the x-api-key header. The payload can be the default JSON or a custom structure; WakeUp Dev normalises the fields and forwards the alert to the appropriate on‑call schedule.
The webhook can also include a routing_key to target a specific team or role, allowing fine‑grained escalation paths.

When the alert is received, WakeUp Dev initiates a Twilio call to the on‑call engineer. The call plays a concise alert summary and waits for a single digit. A TwiML snippet that captures a “1” to acknowledge looks like this:

blocks.code:
<Response>
  <Say voice="alice">Alert: CPU usage exceeded 90%. Press 1 to acknowledge.</Say>
  <Gather numDigits="1" action="/ack" method="POST">
    <Say>Press 1 to acknowledge.</Say>
  </Gather>
  <Say>We did not receive an acknowledgement. Please try again later.</Say>
</Response>

blocks.text: The /ack endpoint records the acknowledgement and updates the alert status in WakeUp Dev’s dashboard. Because the call is the only channel, engineers can focus on the alert without switching contexts.

Traditional on‑call tools charge per seat, which scales poorly for large teams or temporary contractors. WakeUp Dev’s unlimited‑seat model means every engineer can be added to a schedule without additional cost. Coupled with a pay‑per‑alert pricing model, the cost is directly tied to actual usage:

items: **Per‑seat tools**: $5–$10 per seat per month, regardless of alert volume.
**WakeUp Dev**: $0.05 per voice alert, unlimited seats.

blocks.text: This pricing structure aligns incentives: teams pay only for the alerts that matter, and the cost per alert drops as the volume increases.

The combination of low‑latency voice acknowledgement, single‑channel focus, and cost‑effective scaling makes WakeUp Dev a compelling choice for teams that need to keep alert fatigue at bay while staying within budget.
